picks.rationale: Keep the Stafford–Nacua pairing at its verified price; Arizona remains a favorable matchup, while a lopsided Rams win could reduce passing volume.
Keep the Rams backfield anchor. He provides a rushing path alongside the Stafford–Nacua passing pairing; three Rams still concentrate the lineup.
Hall remains ruled out. Keep the replacement lead-back opportunity at $5,700, while treating the road matchup and receiving workload as risks.
Keep the premium Rams receiver rather than weaken the core to spend the last $300. His sourced model estimate remains the highest among the listed receivers.
Keep the Giants receiving anchor. Team reporting confirms that Nabers and Likely both supported substantial production last week; the two selections now share offensive risk.
Keep the $4,000 WR slot with Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek ruled out. Extra opportunity is plausible; a high-volume receiving role is still an assumption.
Keep the $4,100 tight end. The consistent external model still prefers him to the $3,900 Goedert alternative, and switching would not independently fund a core upgrade.
Replace Allgeier with Likely at the same price. Recent target volume and Theo Johnson's confirmed absence support receiving opportunity; do not assume last week's touchdowns repeat.
Keep Pittsburgh at $3,300 with Mayfield ruled out. Backup-quarterback pressure is the thesis; Steelers secondary injuries and return/turnover variance remain risks.

previous_snapshot.note: The two October 17 seed records remain unchanged; this is the first daily run, not a complete week-long trajectory.

revisions.reason: Prefer documented receiving volume at the same price over an early-down replacement whose protection duties and small target share limit the PPR case. The relevant role evidence predates this run; it is newly considered here, not overnight breaking news.

source_qualification_change.description: Official export is now accessible and confirms all selected prices/slots. The seed remains labelled as reported prices with no original full export. No salary correction or silent historical backfill.

projection_comparison.note: Only the 2.7-point selection effect compares the two sets of picks under the same October 18 model snapshot. The older seed estimate stays 134.2; 0.4 of the displayed 3.1-point change comes from model refresh.

strongest_counterargument: The replacement adds a second Giants pass catcher and removes the Arizona bring-back from an already concentrated three-Rams build. New York's two starting tackles remain questionable. Johnson's absence could add blocking duties rather than targets for Likely, and Allgeier could outperform if Arizona's rushing/red-zone workload wins out.
unresolved_assumptions: Final game-day inactives are not yet available; absence of an injury designation is not a guaranteed active status.
Likely keeps a receiving role even if Giants tackle injuries require extra protection.
Bernard's expanded opportunity with Wilson/Skowronek out becomes meaningful targets rather than only more snaps.
The Rams generate enough offense for three selections despite a possible early lead.
Braelon Allen's lead-back role compensates for matchup and receiving uncertainty.
